incidente.resumo: On 19 July 2014 the load on the database of the BBC programme metadata system surged and many metadata requests failed, so products using the metadata directly failed; at almost the same time a pool of the caching layer failed, making BBC iPlayer and the homepage inaccessible. The homepage was put in emergency mode until the cache was stabilised, and remedial work on the metadata system restored close to normal operation for much of the site, while BBC iPlayer was still down on some devices and the full restoration was postponed to Monday morning.
servicos_afetados: audio and video playback on bbc.co.uk

descricao.texto: At 9.30 on Saturday 19 July 2014 the load on the metadata database went through the roof and many requests for metadata to the application servers started to fail; the text does not say how this was noticed.
trechos: At 9.30 on Saturday morning (19th July 2014) the load on the database went through the roof, meaning that many requests for metadata to the application servers started to fail.

descricao.texto: The load on the database of the programme and clip metadata system went through the roof, so many metadata requests to the application servers failed; the source of the additional load is not identified in the text.
trechos: We have a system comprising 58 application servers and 10 database servers that provides programme and clip metadata.
At 9.30 on Saturday morning (19th July 2014) the load on the database went through the roof, meaning that many requests for metadata to the application servers started to fail.

Isolating the source of the additional load proved to be far from straightforward, and restoring the service itself is not as simple as rebooting it (turning it off and on again is the ultimate solution to most problems).

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Some products, mostly older applications, use the metadata directly instead of caching it at the product level, so those products started to fail when metadata requests failed.
trechos: In many cases the metadata is cached at the product level, and can continue to serve content while attempting to revalidate.
In some cases (mostly older applications), the metadata is used directly, and so those products started to fail.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: At almost the same time, one pool of the caching layer in front of most BBC Online products failed, making products including BBC iPlayer and the BBC homepage inaccessible; the failure was complex, repeated a number of times and is still under forensic investigation.
trechos: We use a caching layer in front of most of the products on BBC Online, and one of the pools failed.
The products managed by that pool include BBC iPlayer and the BBC homepage, and the failure made all of those products inaccessible.
The failure was a complex one (we’re still doing the forensics on it), and it has repeated a number of times.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Isolating the source of the additional database load was far from straightforward, and the metadata service could not be restored simply by rebooting it.
trechos: Isolating the source of the additional load proved to be far from straightforward, and restoring the service itself is not as simple as rebooting it (turning it off and on again is the ultimate solution to most problems).

passos.texto: Because of the caching layer failure, the BBC homepage was switched to its emergency simplified mode a number of times during the weekend and finally left up until the cache was completely stabilised.
trechos: It was this failure that resulted in us switching the homepage to its emergency mode (“Due to technical problems, we are displaying a simplified version of the BBC Homepage”).
We used the emergency page a number of times during the weekend, eventually leaving it up until we were confident that we had completely stabilised the cache.

passos.texto: Because performance of the metadata system remained poor, significant remedial work was done on Saturday afternoon into the evening; afterwards the site was in a 'walking wounded' state allowing close to normal operation for much of the site, though BBC iPlayer remained down on a number of devices.
trechos: Performance of the system remained sufficiently poor that in the end we decided to do some significant remedial work on Saturday afternoon, which ran on until the evening.
After that work was complete we were in a walking wounded state that allowed close to normal operation for much of the site, though BBC iPlayer remained down on a number of devices.

acoes.texto: Complete the forensics to fully understand the root causes and put in place measures to minimise the chances of such interruptions in the future.
trechos: We will now be completing the forensics to make sure that we’ve fully understood the root causes, and put in place the measures necessary to minimise the chances of such interruptions in the future.

perguntas_em_aberto: Forensics on the caching layer pool failure are still being done.
The forensics to fully understand the root causes of the incident are still to be completed.

observacoes: The text does not say how the cache pool failure relates to the database load; they are reported as happening at almost the same time and are kept separate. Full restoration of BBC iPlayer was planned for Monday morning (the text gives this as a choice, not as completed), and no end time of the impact is given, so duracao is null. Programmes aired on 12-13 July were unavailable in the catch-up window for some users. causa_raiz.status is vaga, not ausente: the text says what failed (database load went through the roof, making metadata requests fail) but not why the load rose.
